cards.subject: It was jungle
lines: Tanaris was Gurubashi troll country until the Sundering, and the sand took it inside a lifetime.
The goblins did not come for the desert. Steamwheedle built the port and this town together, as a link toward Undermine — and everything else in Gadgetzan is the cost of that one decision.

cards.subject: One of three in the world
lines: Gadgetzan, Booty Bay and Everlook. Nowhere else.
It is the only lawful way an Alliance player and a Horde player can move goods to one another — no trade window, no mail across factions.
The listings sit in their own pool, apart from either side's.

cards.subject: They do not negotiate
lines: Start a fight in town and they converge on it.
In vanilla they are level fifty-seven, which is exactly why a level sixty could kill one, and why people did.
An early patch had to stop the guards attacking you again the moment you resurrected.

cards.subject: The loophole in the middle of town
lines: The walled arena was built for fights where "the bloodier the better", and its walls used to block the guards' line of sight.
So both factions killed each other inside it while the bruisers stood outside, seeing nothing.
A neutral town's most famous feature is the hole in its neutrality.

cards.subject: The inn is called the Road Warrior
cards.tag: And the arena is the Thunderdrome
lines: A walled scrap town in a desert, with a fighting pit and a water monopoly.
It is not accidentally post-apocalyptic.
It is a costume, and somebody put it on deliberately.

cards.subject: The town is here because of wells
lines: A goblin utility drilling across the desert, and the Wastewander bandits took the ones at Waterspring Field.
The company's grievance list reads like a corporate memo: murdered employees, stolen resources, seized property.
Their answer is a bounty board. The water is worth more than the fight.

cards.subject: Nobody is in charge
lines: Booty Bay has Baron Revilgaz on his terrace. Ratchet has Gazlowe. Gadgetzan has neither — no throne, no boss, nobody to petition.
Marin Noggenfogger only becomes baron of this place years later.
Standing here now, he is an alchemist with a stall.

cards.subject: The shopkeeper is the one sounding the alarm
lines: He spends the whole of vanilla analysing insect parts adventurers bring him back from Silithus and Un'Goro.
His conclusion: the silithid are organised under a queen, and something outside them is doing the controlling.
A vendor in a trading post worked out Ahn'Qiraj, and mostly nobody listened.

cards.subject: The pad only receives
cards.tag: You cannot step on it and go anywhere
lines: The device that uses it is an engineering item you trigger from anywhere in the world, and it misfires.
It can turn you into a kobold, a murloc or a troll and freeze you for ten seconds, or stamp an evil twin's face on you for two hours.
Or drop you a hundred yards up, outside town.

cards.subject: A dwarf and an orc, both working
lines: A gryphon master and a wind rider master run this one town, taking money from opposite sides of a war.
The bruisers watch to make sure neither of their customers starts anything.

cards.subject: Four towns, and they talk to each other
lines: Ratchet, Booty Bay, Gadgetzan and Everlook are four separate reputations, and a kill near this town earns you standing here and half as much in each of the other three.
Get friendly enough and the guards will step in on your side.
Neutrality here is a service you can buy up.
